safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 1.85 days

narrative: Material PL2__M4BBB8ED exhibits smooth, approximately normal working-day demand (CV=0.35, 93.8% non-zero) with a statistically significant upward trend (p=0.0002). Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.67) due to a bimodal pattern of short (~1 day) and extended (~3-5 day) replenishments, driven equally by transport and supplier factors. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is recommended: it introduces a 1,428-unit safety stock to cover lead-time and demand variability at 95% service level, and uses a storage-capped order quantity of 6,449 units to reduce ordering frequency and total annual cost by ~85% versus the current SAP baseline.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: unconstrained EOQ of 9,188 units capped to 6,449 units (max_storage_units - safety_stock).
Unstable lead time (CV=0.67): consider supplier SLA consolidation and lead-time monitoring.
Significant upward demand trend detected (p=0.0002): recalibrate policy quarterly.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand (CV=0.35), high non-zero fraction (93.8%), and approximately normal distribution make the classic EOQ-based (r,Q) model the most parsimonious fit. Continuous review is appropriate given frequent daily demand events, and the fixed order quantity minimises total inventory cost subject to the storage cap.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The warehouse capacity of 7,877 units binds the order quantity. If the detected demand trend continues, the effective cycle service level will erode over time. A warehouse capacity review or demand segmentation is advised within 2 quarters.
research_insights.escalation_flag: Lead time instability (CV=0.67) combined with a confirmed demand trend requires quarterly policy recalibration and formal supplier SLA negotiation to reduce lead-time variance.
